fields.name: Tidepool
fields.description: An interactive map of coastal water-quality readings, readable by anyone, not just analysts.

fields.audience: Beachgoers and local volunteers checking whether a beach is safe
fields.problem: The official data is a spreadsheet of station codes and units.
fields.goal: Answer “is it safe today?” in one glance, then let people dig deeper.

fields.ownership: Designed the map, the colour scale and the front end.
fields.team: Small team of three: me on design and front end

fields.approach: One colour and one word per beach, with the raw readings a tap away.
fields.tools: React, MapLibre, a nightly data job, a colour-blind-safe scale.
fields.decisions:
A three-step scale instead of a gradient, because people act on categories.
Open data in, open data out.

fields.challenge: Stations report on different schedules, so the map showed stale and fresh readings side by side.
fields.solution: Show the reading's age on every pin and fade old ones.
fields.tradeoff: A quieter map on slow days, but never a misleading one.

fields.result: Used by a volunteer group for a full summer season.
fields.evidence: Feedback from eleven volunteers; every one found their beach in under ten seconds.
fields.limitations: No formal usability study, and no comparison against the official site.

fields.learned: Honest uncertainty is a design feature.
fields.next_steps: Alerts for a saved beach, and a year-over-year view.
